input.quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 13 binds Clear Capital as well as RadialSpark. It already satisfies most of the fallback: it is mutual, limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, runs only one year post-termination, and is solicitation-based rather than a no-hire. However, it contains no carve-out for general advertising/non-targeted recruiting or for candidate-initiated, unsolicited approaches, which the rule treats as a required element of any acceptable non-solicit. Without it, Clear Capital risks breach merely by hiring a RadialSpark consultant who answers a public job posting. The redline adds the two customary carve-outs and leaves scope and duration untouched, landing the clause at the fallback. Measuring the one-year period from termination rather than from the end of the individual's involvement is a minor variance noted but not redlined.

proposal.summary: Add customary general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs to the mutual non-solicit.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches, since our playbook accepts a non-solicit only where hiring through public job postings or candidate-initiated contact is expressly permitted. The scope and one-year duration are otherwise acceptable to us.

ops.oldText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.newText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Nothing in this Section shall restrict either party from (a) engaging in general advertising or other recruiting efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or from hiring any person who responds to such efforts, or (b) hiring any person who approaches that party on his or her own initiative without solicitation.
